direction_notes: UTS increased spike firing rate of thalamic pyramidal neurons and interneurons and of M1 pyramidal neurons, increased theta-band LFP power in both regions, and increased Granger-causal coupling of LFP between thalamus and M1, indicating direct excitation of the thalamus and indirect (downstream) excitation of M1.

exposures.label: Ultrasonic thalamic stimulation (UTS) of the posterior thalamic nuclear group

timing.protocol_description: Ultrasound was delivered as a single 400 ms stimulation train per trial, with 16 trials per recording session and a 10 s interval between successive stimuli; the firing-rate analysis window ran from 2 s before to 8 s after each UTS trial.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Forty-two C57BL/6 mice were used in these experiments (all male; body weight, 25 g; Beijing Vital River Laboratory Animal Technology $\mathrm { C o . , }$ Ltd China).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The fundamental frequency, stimulation duration, pulsed repetition frequency, and duty cycle were 500 kHz, 400 ms, 1 kHz, and 50%, respectively (figure 1(b)).
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.isppa_w_: The corresponding spatial-peak and pulse-average intensity values were 4.81 W $\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 2 }$ .

flags.reason: Paper states mice were 'randomly divided into two groups' for the thalamus/M1 recording assignment, not that treatment (UTS) vs a control condition was randomised; there is no sham arm in this within-subject before/after design.

Only stimulation duration (400 ms), PRF (1 kHz) and duty cycle (50%) are stated; pulse duration is derivable (duty/PRF) but is never stated explicitly, so it is left not_reported per the no-arithmetic rule.
Methods describe 16 trials per experiment but do not state whether this was one recording session or several; left not_reported.

The 0.38 MPa 'ultrasound intensity' value and the 4.81 W/cm2 Isppa value are not stated as free-field, in-brain/derated, or through-skull; domain is unspecified so both are recorded under unspecified_domain.
